Question: Which of the following sets could NOT be the lengths of the external diagonals of a right rectangular prism [a “box”]? (An external diagonal is a diagonal of one of the rectangular faces of the box.)
Solution:
The three different face-diagonal lengths come from the three pairs of edge lengths. Let the proposed diagonal lengths be \(0<p\le q\le r\). Label the positive box edges \(a,b,c\) so that the faces with diagonals \(p\) and \(q\) share edge \(a\). The Pythagorean theorem gives
\[
p^2=a^2+b^2,\qquad q^2=a^2+c^2,
\]
\[
r^2=b^2+c^2.
\]
Adding the first two equations and subtracting the third eliminates \(b^2\) and \(c^2\):
\[
p^2+q^2-r^2=2a^2>0.
\]
Thus a necessary condition is \(p^2+q^2>r^2\). Equality would force an edge to be zero, which would not give a box.

This condition is also sufficient. Solving the three equations gives
\[
a^2=\frac{p^2+q^2-r^2}{2},
\]
\[
b^2=\frac{p^2+r^2-q^2}{2},\qquad
c^2=\frac{q^2+r^2-p^2}{2}.
\]
The first is positive by the condition. The other two are positive because \(r\ge q\ge p>0\). Taking positive square roots therefore constructs edges whose face diagonals are exactly \(p,q,r\).

For the five choices, the decisive differences are
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{A: }&4^2+5^2-6^2=5,\\
\text{B: }&4^2+5^2-7^2=-8,\\
\text{C: }&4^2+6^2-7^2=3,\\
\text{D: }&5^2+6^2-7^2=12,\\
\text{E: }&5^2+7^2-8^2=10.
\end{aligned}
\]
Only B fails the strict positivity condition. Hence the impossible set is \(\boxed{\{4,5,7\}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
